subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Who murders King Duncan in his sleep?
questions.explain: Macbeth, spurred by the witches' prophecy and Lady Macbeth, stabs the sleeping Duncan in Act 2.

questions.q: How many witches (the Weird Sisters) appear at the start of the play?
questions.explain: The three Weird Sisters open the play and deliver the prophecies that drive Macbeth's ambition.

questions.q: What new title is Macbeth granted after the battle in Act 1, fulfilling the witches' first prophecy?
questions.explain: Duncan rewards Macbeth's valour by making him Thane of Cawdor, exactly as the witches foretold.

questions.q: What is the name of Banquo's son, who escapes the murderers Macbeth sends?
questions.explain: Fleance flees when Banquo is killed, keeping alive the prophecy that Banquo's line will be kings.

questions.q: Who discovers Duncan's murdered body the morning after the killing?
questions.explain: Macduff arrives to wake the king and discovers the murder, raising the alarm in Act 2.

questions.q: Which character cries 'Out, damned spot!' while sleepwalking?
questions.explain: Lady Macbeth's sleepwalking scene shows her guilt as she tries to wash imagined blood from her hands.

questions.q: Who chant the line 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair'?
questions.explain: The Weird Sisters' paradox in Act 1 introduces the theme of appearance versus reality.

questions.q: Who ultimately kills Macbeth in the final battle?
questions.explain: Macduff, 'not of woman born' but delivered by caesarean, slays Macbeth and fulfils the prophecy.

questions.q: When Lady Macbeth demands 'unsex me here', she is asking to be:
options: Stripped of feminine gentleness so she can be cruel
questions.explain: She calls on spirits to remove her womanly compassion so she can help commit murder without remorse.

questions.q: What is the main dramatic function of the witches in the play?
options: To act as loyal servants to Duncan
To plant ambition and set the tragic action in motion
To narrate the plot to the audience
questions.explain: Their prophecies awaken Macbeth's ambition and drive the supernatural, tragic momentum of the play.

questions.q: Lady Macbeth's sleepwalking and obsessive hand-washing most clearly dramatise the theme of:
questions.explain: Her disturbed sleep and imagined bloodstains reveal the crushing guilt she cannot escape.

questions.q: Why does Shakespeare open the play with the witches rather than with Macbeth?
options: To establish an atmosphere of disorder and the supernatural from the outset
To introduce the play's comic subplot
To show the peaceful state of Scotland
questions.explain: The stormy witch scene immediately signals evil, chaos and the supernatural forces shaping the tragedy.

questions.q: How does the play contrast Duncan and Macbeth as kings?
options: Duncan is a gracious, rightful king while Macbeth becomes a bloody tyrant
Macbeth is shown as fairer than Duncan
questions.explain: Duncan's benevolent kingship highlights, by contrast, the tyranny and disorder of Macbeth's usurped reign.

questions.q: Lady Macbeth's advice to 'look like th' innocent flower, But be the serpent under't' develops which idea?
questions.explain: She urges Macbeth to hide murderous intent behind a welcoming face, a recurring appearance-versus-reality motif.

questions.q: In what way does Banquo act as a foil to Macbeth?
options: He is more ambitious than Macbeth
He hears prophecies too but resists acting on them wickedly
He is the one who crowns Macbeth
questions.explain: Banquo receives a prophecy yet stays honourable, throwing Macbeth's moral corruption into relief.

questions.q: The apparition tells Macbeth he is safe 'until Great Birnam Wood to high Dunsinane Hill shall come.' How is this prophecy fulfilled?
options: The wood is set on fire
Malcolm's soldiers cut branches to camouflage their advance
A storm blows the trees down
The witches move the forest by magic
questions.explain: Malcolm's army carries boughs from Birnam Wood towards Dunsinane, making the impossible prophecy literally true.

questions.q: Which quotation best illustrates the theme of destructive ambition?
options: 'Is this a dagger which I see before me'
questions.explain: Macbeth admits his only spur to murder is over-reaching ambition that ultimately causes his downfall.

questions.q: Which line most powerfully conveys Macbeth's guilt immediately after killing Duncan?
options: 'Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood clean from my hand?'
'A little water clears us of this deed'
questions.explain: Macbeth feels his guilt is so vast that no amount of water could ever cleanse the blood from him.

questions.q: If asked to show how Lady Macbeth manipulates her husband, which quotation is the strongest evidence?
options: 'Here's the smell of the blood still'
questions.explain: She pressures a hesitant Macbeth to steel his nerve and go through with Duncan's murder.

questions.q: Macbeth's speech 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow' is best used as evidence of his:
options: Nihilistic despair as his world collapses
questions.explain: Learning of Lady Macbeth's death, Macbeth expresses a bleak view that life is meaningless and futile.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) English Literature (J352) specification; Macbeth
